subject.title: fix(reef): contain startup friend reconcile failures

question: Should Reef remain running after a retryable startup friend-reconcile failure, using persisted peer keys until the next retry, rather than fail startup and trigger supervisor restarts?
rationale: This is an intentional availability-versus-message-delivery tradeoff; tests prove the mechanics, but they cannot determine whether briefly stale peer keys are the accepted production policy.

options.title: Accept bounded degraded startup
options.body: Keep the proposed retry classification and permit startup with persisted peer keys, relying on the next reconciliation interval to refresh them.

options.title: Keep fail-closed startup
options.body: Reject retryable startup reconcile failures so activation waits for a successful peer-key refresh, accepting the existing restart behavior until a different recovery design is approved.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded degraded startup
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed retry classification and permit startup with persisted peer keys, relying on the next reconciliation interval to refresh them.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Reef recovery work and the branch’s recovery-hardening commit connect this decision most directly to steipete.
